To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

model-based Bayesian reinforcement-learning methods can be successfully applied in the domain of human–robot interaction, that they are particularly well suited to handle the uncertainty of the model, and that they can be improved by using a structured representation of the interaction dynamics.

model-based Bayesian reinforcement learn- ing can be successfully used for dialogue policy optimisation in human–robot interac- tion, that a structured model representation with probabilistic rules can be beneficial in this context, and that the approach can be used to improve dialogue management in a Wizard-of-Oz user simulator.
model-based Bayesian reinforcement-learning methods for dialogue management can be effective and can benefit from incorporating prior domain knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a principled Bayesian approach to model-based dialogue policy learning.
the development of model-based Bayesian reinforcement-learning techniques for dialogue management in spoken dialogue systems.
the design of a model-based reinforcement learning framework that can learn to adapt its behaviour in a dynamic environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is very promising, but that it is still too early for a definite evaluation.
the model-based Bayesian approach to dialogue management is a promising direction for future work, which is supported by our empirical findings.
the Bayesian approach with rules outperforms the other two approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the potential of Bayesian inference for dialogue policy optimisation and that we have shown that a structured model representation with probabilistic rules can be beneficial in this context.
the model-based Bayesian approach can achieve better learning performance than model-free approaches in terms of the average reward and the number of interactions required for convergence.
we have shown that Bayesian reinforcement learning is a promising direction for the development of dialogue policies in interactive systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Bayesian inference can be a promising strategy for model-based reinforcement learning in dialogue systems, and can help in the design of more robust agents.
Bayesian inference can be used to maintain an explicit model of the environment while simultaneously planning the actions to be taken in a reinforcement learning scenario.
model-based Bayesian reinforcement methods can be used to efficiently learn dialogue policies from experience.
